title: Testis and epididymis: microscopic anatomy
description: The sperm-production organ from tunica through seminiferous tubule to rete, efferent ducts and epididymal tail.

questions.question: Where are sperm made in the testis?
questions.answer: Sperm develop within seminiferous tubules. Supporting Sertoli cells and hormone-producing interstitial Leydig cells occupy different microscopic compartments.

questions.question: How do sperm leave the testis?
questions.answer: They move from seminiferous tubules through a collecting network and efferent ductules into the epididymis, where maturation and storage continue.

questions.question: What is the tunica vaginalis?
questions.answer: Serous covering with visceral and parietal layers. Function: Allows mobile testis within scrotum.

questions.question: Where is the mediastinum testis located?
questions.answer: Posterior thickening of albuginea containing rete testis. Function: Organizes lobules and duct outflow.

questions.question: What is the function of the seminiferous tubules?
questions.answer: Function: Spermatogenesis. Coiled tubules lined by developing germ cells and Sertoli cells.
